title: Self Feeding for Toddlers: Simple Tips for Letting Little Ones Feed Themselves
description: Self-feeding is slow and messy, and that's normal. Cut food into pieces they can pick up, put a spoon on the tray even if they ignore it, and sit at their level instead of hovering. A wipeable floor and a damp cloth nearby take a lot of the stress out of it for the grown-ups.

title: Infant Room Book Corner: How to Set Up a Reading Space for Babies
description: Babies choose books by the cover, so face them out on a low display instead of shelving them spine first. Keep board and cloth books in reach, put out only a few at a time, and leave a soft spot where a grown-up can sit with a baby or two on their lap. title: Snack Time in Daycare: Simple Ways to Keep Toddler Snack Time Calm
description: In group care, snack goes better when children sit close enough to see each other. They watch and copy. Seat them side by side, keep portions small so they can ask for more, give them real cups with only a little in them, and stay sitting with them for the whole snack.

description: Babies use a low shelf by pulling everything off it, so plan for that. Put out a few light baskets, each with one kind of thing: wooden rings, three soft balls, fabric squares. A mirror-back cubby gives crawlers something to look into at floor level. Leave open floor in front for sitting and dumping. As an Amazon Associate, Yalla earns from qualifying purchases.

title: Picky Eating in Toddlers: Gentle Ways to Offer New Foods Without Pressure
description: Lots of toddlers turn down a new food many times before they try it. Put a small piece on the plate next to something they already like, eat it yourself where they can see, and skip the bribes and the "one more bite." If the broccoli comes back untouched, that's fine. Offer it again another day.
